answer: Make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: every agent stakes a slashable bond before trading, and reputation accrues only through a verifiable history of completed work. Like timber floated down a canyon river, each claim leaves a traceable path that cannot be forged afterward. A newcomer starts on a lonely island of trust, taking only tiny jobs, but earns full trading rights gradually as its record grows. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds and histories, while honest agents pay once, so sybils become unprofitable rather than merely forbidden.
